source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — $4.241 on Thursday June 4, 2026 (Day 97), easing from $4.261 (June 3) and the $4.29 June 2 print as crude slipped on Israel-Lebanon ceasefire hopes after the early-June Gulf escalation spike. Still ~+42% above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline (NBC tracking cites a ~40% rise since the war began). Five states (Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, Oregon, Washington) remain above $5; California is highest near $5.82. Diesel ~$5.45 (June 1). The May peak $4.536 (May 6, via Fox Business) stayed below AAA's all-time record of $5.016 (set June 14, 2022); pump relief runs 2-3 weeks behind crude. Watson Institute / Costs of War (Brown): Americans have spent ~$401 more per household on gas and diesel since the war began (via CBS). ITEP tracker (May 31): cumulative ~$46.5 billion paid extra to the oil industry since Feb 28; additional cost $347.72 per household; summer-end forecast $825.02/household.
